source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin AUS2-AUS3 campus publishes 19 MW of IT load across 242,000 square feet of technical space, a mid-sized facility whose certifications point to regulated tenants rather than AI training at scale.

Within Texas, the campus ranks tenth by published capacity among the 19 state facilities that disclose a figure. Its 19 MW equals 4 percent of the 475 MW of published IT load statewide. Texas maps 133 data center facilities in total, so most publish nothing, and that tenth-place standing describes a disclosed subset rather than actual regional supply.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, qualify the site for financial, healthcare and federal workloads. Those tenants compete for the same megawatts that AI training wants, and compliance obligations decide who can occupy the space. At 19 MW the campus sits below the scale of hyperscale AI hubs, so it is more plausibly a compliance and colocation site than a frontier training site.

Published IT load is a ceiling, not availability. The record does not include power delivery headroom for GPU densities above legacy IT, grid interconnection quality, or any announced expansion, and the suitability score of 62 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type. It also carries no address, no coordinates and no nearest airport, so the facility cannot be tied to a specific substation or transmission constraint from this data alone.
